correctness.rationale: A strict proper-suffix criterion classifies all binary Lyndon subsequences of the four-run input as either \(0^i1^j\) or \(0^i1^j0^k1^l\) with \(i>k\) or \(i=k,j<l\). Maximization over positive exponents yields the exact deficiency formula, with edge cases \(a=c=1\) and \(b\ge d\) handled by deleting the one-symbol middle zero run. Two disjoint generating-function sums for \(b<d\) and \(b\ge d\) give the marked rational distribution. A sharp linear extremum is attained explicitly; uniform composition convergence and an exactly integrated Dirichlet tail give the limit law. Finite independent checks exhaust 625 complete subsequence sets and all 91,390 compositions of lengths 4..40; those checks are not treated as infinite proof. The argument and its boundaries are in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The full accessible Algorithmica article on longest Lyndon subsequences gives general cubic-time algorithms and a unique-character special case, but does not state the exact positive four-run length deficiency, its bivariate rational distribution or its Dirichlet limiting law. Direct searches for the same invariant, run parameters and probabilistic aliases found no equivalent table or claim; an unindexed equivalent specialization remains a documented risk, not claimed disproved. Distinct earlier Lyndon substring and Lyndon-factor results do not imply scattered optimal length. The general algorithm can compute each instance but does not give this four-parameter formula and statistical law. The complete 2021 Hirakawa et al. preprint counts Lyndon subsequences by occurrence and distinctness, and contains no fixed-word longest-length theorem; this distinct-statistic comparison does not establish absolute priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed literature or a detailed unpublished calculation might independently contain an equivalent run-length formula or distribution.

value.rationale: Longest Lyndon scattered subsequences are a named algorithmic invariant whose general polynomial-time computation was a research target. Positive four-run binary words are the smallest family with an internal 0/1 conflict while still admitting a full-word Lyndon case. The formula converts the general string problem to \(O(1)\) arithmetic on a run-length representation and gives a complete family classification. The rational bivariate distribution, sharp worst-case deletion loss and explicit mixed atomic/continuous Dirichlet limit are nontrivial intrinsic enumerative facts relevant to compressed-string statistics, not just one-off instances, substitutions or finite enumeration.
